prompt: A new platoon sergeant asks the supply and motor pool sections whether they will support the platoon's mission. Which item on the list for assuming a leadership position is this?
options: Determine what your organization expects of you
Determine who your immediate leader is and what they expect
Identify the key points outside the organization whose willing support is needed
Determine the competence, strengths and weaknesses of your soldiers
explanation: Slide 16, item 4: identify the key points outside the organization whose willing support is needed to accomplish the mission.

prompt: A new NCO asks how the mission fits in with the mission of the next higher organization. Which other question appears on the same list?
options: What resources are available to help the organization accomplish the mission?
Who approves the non-judicial punishment imposed on enlisted soldiers in the unit?
Which disciplinary measures did the previous NCO use?
Which soldiers were promoted last year?
explanation: Slide 16 lists the next higher organization's mission question together with the question on available resources.

prompt: Which statement about assuming a leadership position is correct?
options: It is a situation faced only by NCOs who hold the rank of First Sergeant
It is one of the most important leadership situations that may face an NCO
It is complete once the NCO has learned the unit's mission
It is handled by the chain of command on behalf of the NCO
explanation: Slide 15 calls assuming a leadership position one of the most important leadership situations that may face an NCO.

prompt: Which pairing of counts matches the lesson?
options: Twelve things to think about when assuming a leadership position, and thirteen broad categories in the NCO 'Bible'
Nine things to think about when assuming a leadership position, and twelve broad categories in the NCO 'Bible'
Thirteen things to think about when assuming a leadership position, and ten broad categories in the NCO 'Bible'
Thirteen things to think about when assuming a leadership position, and twelve broad categories in the NCO 'Bible'
explanation: Slides 15-17 number thirteen items for assuming a leadership position, and slides 26-27 list twelve broad categories of the NCO 'Bible'.

prompt: An NCO is ordered by the commander to supervise a flag ceremony, which is not in his job description. To keep his own radio ready, he also tests his cables each morning without being told. Which duty types are these, in order?
options: Directed duty, then implied duty
Specified duty, then directed duty
Implied duty, then specified duty
Directed duty, then specified duty
explanation: Slide 22: an other-directed task outside the job is a directed duty, while a task that supports a specified duty without being assigned is an implied duty.

prompt: A soldier skips a required check, and supervisors ignore a known recurring gap. Which pair of responsibility categories applies?
options: Command responsibility for the soldier and individual responsibility for the supervisors
Individual responsibility for both the soldier and the supervisors
Individual responsibility for the soldier and command responsibility for the supervisors
Command authority for the soldier and general military authority for the supervisors
explanation: Slide 24: individual responsibility concerns each soldier's own performance, while command responsibility concerns how well the unit performs.

prompt: A sergeant has the right to direct his squad by virtue of assignment, yet the squad fails its mission. Which pairing fits?
options: General military authority for the right to direct, individual responsibility for the failure
Command authority for the right to direct, command responsibility for the failure
Command responsibility for the right to direct, command authority for the failure
Specified duty for the right to direct, directed duty for the failure
explanation: Slides 24 and 29: command authority comes from rank or assignment, while command responsibility is accountability for unit performance.

prompt: A squad leader checks the serviceability of rifles and vehicles and the condition of billets and work areas. Which two NCO categories does this reflect?
options: Individual training in MOS, and supervision of subordinates
Communication between soldier and organization, and advice on policy to the chain of command
Physical and mental well-being of the soldier, and planning of day-to-day operations
Maintenance and accountability of equipment, and appearance and condition of billets, facilities, and work areas
explanation: Slide 27 lists maintenance and accountability of arms, vehicles and equipment (10) and appearance and condition of billets, facilities, and work areas (11).

prompt: A platoon sergeant gives lawful orders to his own platoon. Which statement about the source of this authority is correct?
options: It originates with the President and may be supplemented by law or regulation
It arises from the absence of a designated leader
It is extended to all soldiers regardless of assignment
It derives from the soldier's own responsibility to improve his performance and do his job well
explanation: Slide 29: command authority, held by virtue of rank or assignment, originates with the President.

prompt: Which statement correctly distinguishes inspections from corrections?
options: Inspections address the deficiencies found, while corrections evaluate adherence to standards
Inspections evaluate adherence to standards, while corrections address the deficiencies found
Both are conducted only to impose disciplinary measures
Corrections must come before inspections can be conducted
explanation: Slides 30-31: inspections are systematic evaluations of adherence to standards; corrections are actions taken to address deficiencies.

prompt: A soldier's deficiency is addressed with corrective training after normal duty hours. Which statement follows the guidelines?
options: It becomes punishment because it is after normal duty hours
It must continue until the next formal inspection
It may be unrelated to the deficiency if all soldiers take part
It remains training or instruction, not punishment
explanation: Slide 34: corrective measures after normal duty hours assume the nature of training or instruction, not punishment.

prompt: A sergeant tells a soldier that he is a lazy person because his uniform is wrong. Which on-the-spot correction step was violated?
options: Attack the performance, never the person
Correct the soldier
Give one correction at a time
Don't keep bringing it up
explanation: Slides 33 and 36: the correction must attack the performance, never the person.

prompt: A leader checks soldiers' gear in formation, and the next day checks readiness before a patrol. Which inspections are these, in order?
options: In-quarters inspection, then on-the-spot correction
On-the-spot inspection, then in-ranks inspection
In-ranks inspection, then PCC/PCI
PCC/PCI, then in-quarters inspection
explanation: Slides 32 and 35: in-ranks inspections are held in a unit formation, and PCCs/PCIs prepare soldiers before execution.

prompt: A soldier fails to maintain his weapon properly. Which corrective training follows the guidelines?
options: Extra guard duty for the whole squad until the next inspection
Weapon maintenance instruction aimed at his problem area
Barracks cleaning until the next inspection
A long run for the whole platoon
explanation: Slide 34: corrective training must be directly related to the deficiency and oriented to the soldier's problem area.

prompt: Which sequence matches an informal unscheduled check, a readiness check before operations, and training aimed at a deficiency?
options: In-ranks inspection, PCC/PCI, on-the-spot correction
PCC/PCI, on-the-spot inspection, corrective training
On-the-spot inspection, PCC/PCI, corrective training
On-the-spot inspection, corrective training, PCC/PCI
explanation: Slides 34-35 define the on-the-spot inspection as informal and unscheduled, PCC/PCI as readiness checks, and corrective training as aimed at the deficiency.

prompt: Which statement correctly describes the NCO support channel and the chain of command?
options: It replaces the formal chain of command in day-to-day operations and enlisted matters of the unit
It acts independently of prescribed policies and directives
It limits its work to advising on officers' concerns
It complements the formal chain of command by addressing enlisted needs and concerns
explanation: Slide 37: the channel complements the formal chain of command by addressing the specific needs and concerns of enlisted personnel.

prompt: Which pair of functions are both listed ways the NCO support channel assists the chain of command?
options: Teaching soldiers the unit's mission and administering the NCO professional development program
Approving individual training programs for officers and setting the standards of conduct for the unit
Advising on officer promotions and issuing unit policy
Replacing commanders in training and supervising officers' fitness
explanation: Slide 39 lists teaching soldiers the mission of the unit and administering and monitoring the NCO professional development program.

prompt: A team leader checks on a soldier's family problem, both on and off duty. Which support channel function does this show?
options: Advising the commander on rewards and punishment
Caring for individual soldiers and their families
Supervising unit physical fitness training
Teaching soldiers the history of the Philippine Army
explanation: Slide 39: the channel cares for individual soldiers and their families both on and off duty.

prompt: Which statement about the NCO support channel is correct?
options: It sets the Philippine Army ethic independently of the chain of command and the commander's directives
It limits training to basic skills taught by officers
It supervises soldiers only while they are on duty
It transmits, instills and ensures the efficacy of the professional Philippine Army ethic
explanation: Slide 38 lists transmitting, instilling and ensuring the efficacy of the professional Philippine Army ethic as the first function.

prompt: A first sergeant is asked to plan and conduct day-to-day unit operations. Within what limits does the support channel do this?
options: Within limits set by each section for itself
Within the approval of the platoon leader only
Within prescribed policies and directives
Without reference to the commander's policy
explanation: Slide 38: the channel plans and conducts day-to-day unit operations within prescribed policies and directives.
